newsitem.title: USA: Simpson expected back on witness stand Friday.
newsitem.headline: Simpson expected back on witness stand Friday.

text.p: O.J. Simpson will return to the witness stand Friday for his second round of testimony in his civil trial, one of his attorneys said Tuesday.
Attorneys said closing arguments in the wrongful-death civil case could begin as early as Jan. 17, depending on the scheduling of the remaining witnesses.

Simpson testified for the first time in late November after being called to the witness stand by the plaintiffs' lawyers, who subjected him to three days of harsh interrogation. He is expected Friday to be face gentler questioning by his own defence attorneys.

Simpson was acquitted in October 1995 of criminal charges in the June 12, 1994, murders of his ex-wife, Nicole Brown Simpson, and her friend, Ronald Goldman. He is now battling a civil suit brought by the victims' families, who are seeking monetary damages.
The jury was given the day off Tuesday so that one of the panellists could observe a religious holiday.
But during a court hearing to discuss the scheduling of witnesses, Phillip Baker, one of Simpson's attorneys, said the former football star would take the witness stand Friday.
Simpson's defence team said they wanted to begin closing arguments on Jan. 17, but the plaintiffs' attorneys asked Judge Hiroshi Fujisaki to wait until Jan. 21. The judge said he would decide later.
Simpson's lawyers plan to rest their case next Monday after testimony by his adult daughter, Arnelle, and possibly several other witnesses.
Lawyers in the case Tuesday also hammered out legal issues related to the upcoming videotaped testimony of Dr. Henry Lee, an expert in forensic science retained by the defence.

The jury is scheduled to return to court Wednesday to hear testimony by Simpson's former houseguest, Brian "Kato" Kaelin, and several other witnesses, possibly including Simpson's close friend, Al Cowlings.
Defence lawyers hope to introduce a videotape of Lee's testimony on Thursday.
